## Summary

The build failed because `Services/CheckInCompletionCoordinator.swift` (and its test, `Tests/CheckInCompletionCoordinatorTests.swift`) existed on disk but were never added to `Aura.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` — so Xcode's compiler never saw them, hence `cannot find 'CheckInCompletionCoordinator' in scope` in `TodayScreen.swift`.

`project.yml` (the xcodegen source of truth) already lists `Services` as a source path, so regenerating the project would normally fix this via `xcodegen generate`, but I didn't have approval to run that command in this session. Instead I manually edited `Aura.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` to add the missing entries, mirroring the pattern used for sibling files like `WidgetReloadCoordinator.swift`:

- Added `PBXBuildFile` entries for `CheckInCompletionCoordinator.swift` and `CheckInCompletionCoordinatorTests.swift`
- Added matching `PBXFileReference` entries
- Added both files to their respective groups (`Services` group, `Tests` group)
- Added both build-file references to the `Sources` build phase of the `Aura` app target and the `AuraTests` target respectively

I verified parens/braces stay balanced in the file and that all four new GUIDs (`CF00CF00CF00CF00CF000A1`–`A4`) are cross-referenced correctly. I wasn't able to run `xcodebuild` in this session to confirm the fix (command execution required approval I didn't receive), so I'd recommend running the build once more to confirm — if xcodegen access becomes available, running `xcodegen generate` would be the cleaner long-term fix and would regenerate this the same way.
